job_description:

Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

A Day in the Life
We are seeking a committed professional to join our team. While this is a remote position not located at a physical Medtronic site, the candidate hired will be required to reside within the territory and drive to multiple accounts throughout the region. A valid driver's license is essential for this role.

As one of three comprehensive portfolios at Medtronic, Neuroscience is dedicated to improving the lives of people living with neurological disorders, spine conditions, and chronic pain. Guided by our Mission—to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life—we develop technologies and therapies that help people regain function, reduce pain, and return to the activities that matter most.

Medtronic Pelvic Health provides therapies that treat patients suffering from overactive bladder, non-obstructive urinary retention and fecal incontinence with our sacral neuromodulation (SNM) systems InterStim X™️ and InterStim™️ Micro; and our percutaneous tibial neuromodulation (PTNM) system NURO™️. More than 400 million people worldwide have incontinence, and many of them limit their lives socially, professionally and personally because of their condition. Our goal is to expand access to our therapies, and introduce new therapies, so we can potentially help millions of people get their lives back.

As a Pelvic Health Therapy Development Specialist, you will play a critical role in the successful introduction and adoption of new OAB (overactive bladder) therapies. You will provide in-depth technical support and guidance to help HCP teams build confidence, capability and belief in our innovative new therapies. The ideal candidate will be energized by the opportunity to partner with HCPs to offer new therapies and motivated to expand access for patients. You will possess a strong background in medical device technology, possess product and procedure expertise, therapy development experience, a strong track record of agility and adaptability to learn, and the ability to manage and collaborate with complex stakeholders and build effective working relationships.

This role will require 50+% travel within the assigned district and potentially outside of the district as business needs dictate.

Primary Responsibilities:

Therapy Implementation

· Own the customer implementation process and procedural success metrics to drive adoption of new Pelvic Health therapies within targeted accounts. Set a strong foundation for customer and procedural independence and program growth

· Guide medical professionals to safely and effectively use new therapies including, but not limited to, implant and technologies that enable procedure success.   Provide education and technical support to HCPs to enhance their understanding, usage, and long-term adoption of new therapies

· Identify implementation and broader adoption challenges and determine the most appropriate avenue for resolution

· Conduct reviews with HCP teams to provide metrics on implementation status, discuss successes and address any challenges.  Gather and analyze feedback from physicians and clinician teams to identify areas for improvement, optimization, and long-term adoption

· Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including marketing, sales, and product development, to ensure a successful product launch

​

Market Development

· Partner with District Manager, Marketing, Medical Education and Field Market Development to identify current and future needs related to procedure market development at targeted accounts

· Develop and execute therapy development plans for each target account to support sustained adoption

​

Customer Relationship Management

· Build and maintain strong relationships with HCP and staff at supported sites

· Act as a liaison between the company and healthcare provider teams to address any concerns or questions related to new products

​

Case Coverage

· Provide on-site technical support during initial procedures to ensure the proper use

· Assist physicians and clinical staff with technical guidance and troubleshooting during procedures

· Ensure compliance with all safety protocols and guidelines during product usage in the OR/ASC/Office

​

​Clinical expertise

· Stay up to date on latest clinical publications

· Attend at least 1 physician training – potentially supports cadaver portion of that training

· In accordance with applicable Medtronic policies and procedures, share new support materials (e.g. case publications, case libraries, etc.) with HCPs

· Share insights and best practices with internal teams

​

Continuous Improvement

· Stay updated on the latest advancements in relevant technology and surgical techniques

· Participate in ongoing training and professional development opportunities to enhance skills and knowledge

· Contribute to the continuous improvement of training programs and technical support processes

​

​Required Qualifications:

High School Diploma (or equivalent) AND 8+ years relevant sales, clinical, or related experience in medical devices, medtech, healthcare, or life sciences OR Associate’s Degree AND 6+ years relevant sales, clinical, or related experience in medical devices, medtech, healthcare, or life sciences OR Bachelor’s Degree AND 4+ years relevant sales, clinical, or related experience in medical devices, medtech, healthcare, or life sciences

​

Preferred Qualifications:

Advanced degree or certification in a relevant field

Experience with product launch and market introduction of medical devices

Proven track record of successful physician training and/or case coverage

Strong understanding of surgical procedures and medical device technology

Confidence to provide physician constructive feedback to improve performance

Ability to work independently and collaborate with cross-functional partners to assess and address barriers to full adoption

Ability to manage change in a way that reduces the concern experienced by others

For Baccalaureate degrees earned outside of the United States, a degree that satisfies the requirements of 8 C.F.R. § 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A) is required.

募集職種：Principal Marketing Specialist ｜ 所属：Surgical / Specialty Development

Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

A Day in the Life
At Medtronic, we bring bold ideas forward with speed and decisiveness to put patients first in everything we do. In-person exchanges are invaluable to our work. We’re working onsite 5 days a week as part of our commitment to fostering a culture of professional growth and cross-functional collaboration as we work together to engineer the extraordinary.

The Senior Quality Systems Specialist will serve as the primary interface between Medtronic and external customers for a designated business, while owning and optimizing the Quality Management System (QMS) processes that support customer-related activities. This role combines hands-on customer support (orders, changes, complaints, RMAs) with end-to-end responsibility for designing, maintaining, and improving quality processes, metrics, and documentation in alignment with ISO 13485 and FDA requirements.

Responsibilities may include the following and other duties may be assigned.

Customer-Focused Quality Systems and Process Ownership

Optimize and enhance existing Tempe Medtronic frameworks that support customer-related activities to ensure alignment with ISO 13485, FDA requirements, and internal quality system standards.

Establish, track, and continuously improve metrics and measurable indicators for customer-related processes (e.g., order performance, complaints, returns, turnaround times, service quality).

Create, maintain, and revise QMS documentation (procedures, work instructions, forms, templates) required to support customer-related processes.

Ensure audit readiness for customer-related quality processes and act as the subject matter expert (SME) during internal, external, and regulatory audits.

Work with cross-functional and quality teams to develop, implement, and refine methods for collecting and reporting customer feedback and quality data.

Customer Interface and Order Management

Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned external customers, working with local groups on coordinating orders, changes, issue resolution, feedback/complaints, returns, and requests.

Work with local planning team to accept forecasts and purchase orders from customers and create corresponding sales orders in SAP.

Provide clear order acknowledgements to customers, leveraging SAP functionality where available and supporting configuration needs for the site as appropriate.

Collaborate with Planning to obtain and confirm commit dates and communicate commitments to customers.

Monitor drop shipments and coordinate with Planning to define transaction ownership (Planning vs. this role) in MES and SAP to ensure accurate shipment execution and documentation.

Ensure SAP shipment transactions are completed accurately to generate invoices and shipping paperwork required by customers.

Change Management and Customer Portals

Partner with Engineering and other internal stakeholders to understand and execute customer-requested changes (e.g., product, documentation, process, or configuration changes).

Submit and manage changes through customer change portals, acting as a liaison to reduce administrative burden on Engineering and other technical teams.

Support equipment changes, engineering changes, new equipment introduction, and manufacturing process improvements.

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical/scientific discipline.

Previous experience or demonstrated knowledge in a manufacturing engineering, validation, quality engineering, or calibration environment.

Understanding of manufacturing equipment, measurement systems, and engineering documentation.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

Ability to work effectively in a cross-functional manufacturing environment.

Good written and verbal communication skills.

English proficiency sufficient to work with technical documentation and global engineering teams.

Ability to work onsite in Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua, Mexico.

Experience in medical device manufacturing or another highly regulated manufacturing environment.

Knowledge of ISO 13485 and regulated medical-device manufacturing requirements. These are also identified as preferred capabilities in the internal Manufacturing Engineer profile.

Experience preparing or executing IQ/OQ/PQ validation protocols and reports.

Experience with Test Method Validation (TMV).

Knowledge of measurement systems, calibration principles, MSA, and Gage R&R.

Familiarity with pFMEA, CAPA, nonconformance investigations, change control, and root cause analysis.

Experience using statistical tools such as Minitab for process or validation analysis.

Experience preparing and submitting environmental regulatory reports (examples include EPCRA reporting, Annual Air Emissions Summary, DMRs, SMRs)

Virtual design and prototyping of new implants, delivery systems, or single-use devices used for peripheral intervention. Application of CFD or FSI software tools to predict flow conditions related to peripheral vascular interventions

Experience in the application of the principles of fatigue analysis for metals including superelastic and shape memory alloys. Simulation of highly deformed metals, polymers, fabrics, biological tissue and pulsatile flow conditions

Demonstrated proactive creation of novel algorithms and scripts to automate post-process finite element output databases

Exposure to the development of novel model validation experiments and analogous finite element modelling, and development of material testing protocols to calibrate constitutive models, as well as FEA model validation. Bachelor’s degree in Materials Science, Engineering Mechanics, Mechanical Engineering, Physics or related technical discipline.

Knowledge of engineering mechanics, mechanical design, material processing, fatigue analysis, metallurgy and strength of materials.

Knowledge and experience with application of technical principles, theories, and design concepts in implantable product design including product, process, and technology development and evaluation.

Knowledge of risk management analysis including Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and statistical techniques relevant for design and test for reliability.

Own the strategy, roadmap, governance, and continuous improvement of Adobe Creative Cloud, Adobe Acrobat, and Shutterstock, ensuring effective licensing, access management, integrations, platform adoption, change management, and alignment of product capabilities with business needs and objectives

Represents the electrical engineering team within the RF generator workstream.

Program and Workstream Leadership

Manage schedules and dependencies in collaboration with R&D lead and Project Management Office partners.

Perform day‑to‑day management of technical priorities, tradeoffs, and issue resolution within the workstream.

Support planning for electrical engineering spend, resourcing, tools, and equipment.

Serve as primary owner for identification, assessment, and communication of electrical and system‑level risks and emerging issues.

Champion consistent application of the quality system, design controls, and best practices across electrical engineering activities.

Ensure solutions comply with regulatory, safety, and reliability requirements for medical devices.

Ensure strong cross‑functional alignment across systems, software, manufacturing, quality, and program teams.

Translate electrical design intent and requirements to manufacturing partners to ensure producibility and design transfer readiness.

Provide regular and ad‑hoc technical and program updates to functional and program leadership.

Proactively communicate emerging issues, escalations, and risk status to CTM and other stakeholders.

Provide technical guidance, coaching, and mentorship to engineers across the organization.

Influence engineering standards, best practices, and continuous improvement initiatives to mature electrical engineering capability.

Electromechanical Systems / Capital equipment, or equivalent experience including hardware and software integration

Technical leadership experience

A Day in the Life
We are pioneering the future of medical diagnostics with our innovative capsule endoscopy solutions. Imagine a world where diagnosing gastrointestinal conditions is as simple as swallowing a pill which captures with imagers and different sensors the digestive system and transmit it in real time. Our cutting-edge technology not only makes this possible but also revolutionizes the patient experience, providing a non-invasive, accurate, and efficient diagnostic tool. We are seeking a dynamic and visionary Analog and RF engineer to join our dedicated team, driving the development and integration of our next-generation capsule endoscopy devices.

As a Senior Analog & RF Engineer specializing in capsule endoscopy development, you will play a key role in the design, development, and integration of the critical analog and RF communication path between the capsule, located inside the patient’s digestive system, and the external recorder worn by the patient.
You will be responsible for developing high-performance, low-power analog and RF solutions that enable reliable wireless communication, contributing directly to the performance and advancement of our next-generation medical devices.
In this critical role, you will collaborate closely with System Engineers, PCB design and Layout, Firmware Developers, Modem Algorithm Engineers, and Mechanical Design teams to develop and integrate advanced solutions across the system. You will work in a highly collaborative, open-minded environment that encourages new ideas, creativity, and innovation, contributing to cutting-edge medical technology that enhances patient care.

Primary responsibilities:

Own and drive the Analog & RF communication path from architecture definition through detailed design.

Work closely with leading semiconductor suppliers and technology partners on a system on Chip definition, development, and integration of custom IC/ASIC solutions, contributing to system architectural decisions and ensuring alignment with system-level requirements.

Research, evaluate, and define communication receiver and transmitter architectures, including Zero-IF, Low-IF/NZ-IF, Superheterodyne, and other relevant architectures, based on system requirements and product constraints.

Perform system-level RF and Analog analysis, including noise budget, link budget, dynamic range, sensitivity, linearity, distortion, interference, and overall communication-channel performance.

Develop simulation models and methodologies to evaluate communication-channel performance and validate architectural and design decisions prior to hardware implementation.

Design and specify the Analog transmitter and receiver signal paths, including filtering, amplification, gain stages, matching networks.

Analyse and optimize antenna design and RF performance, including antenna matching, efficiency, radiation characteristics, impedance, and interaction with the capsule and surrounding biological environment.

Drive a system on chip designs from proof-of-concept and laboratory prototypes into production-ready medical devices.

Required qualifications:

BSc \ MSc in Electrical Engineering.

7+ years of hands-on experience in very Low power Analog and RF engineering, preferably in wireless communication systems, RFICs, or mixed-signal systems; Familiarity with SoC/mixed-signal architecture, including considerations for integrating analog, RF, digital, and power-management functions.

Strong understanding of RF and analog communication architectures, including Zero-IF, Low-IF/NZ-IF, Superheterodyne, and related receiver/transmitter architectures; Proven experience with analog/RF transmitter and receiver design, including filters, amplifiers, LNAs, PAs, mixers, matching networks, and signal-conditioning circuits; Strong understanding of PCB-level RF implementation, including layout, grounding, shielding, power integrity, signal integrity, and RF isolation.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience in writing design and technical specifications.

Experience in Simulation techniques both transmitter and receiver performance as well as Antenna simulation; Experience in Lab measurement equipment and lab work.

Familiarity with board design , medical equipment development process, RF Compliance standards.

The Extrusion Operator sets up and operates plastic extrusion equipment used to manufacture miniature, precision tubing. Set up and operate plastic extrusion equipment to manufacture miniature, precision tubing to established quality standards.

Monitor extrusion processes using knowledge of resin characteristics, temperature control, automated feedback loops, and screw and tool design.

Operate ancillary downstream equipment, including burst testers and slickers.

Troubleshoot, repair, and perform maintenance on extrusion equipment.

Support engineering in the development of extrusion tooling, equipment, and materials.

Write and execute equipment qualifications for new or modified tooling and equipment, documenting that operations meet established parameters.

Experience with plastic extrusion equipment and processes.

Experience with precision tubing manufacturing.

Knowledge of extrusion tooling, screw and tool design, and resin characteristics.

Experience with temperature controls, automated feedback loops, and downstream extrusion equipment.

Experience troubleshooting or maintaining extrusion equipment.

A Day in the Life

Contexte

Les chirurgies de réparation des hernies sont de plus en plus réalisées par voie laparoscopique ou robotique, ce qui nécessite l’introduction d’implants textiles de renfort pariétal à travers des trocarts. La recherche d’approches moins invasives, au bénéfice du patient, favorise l’utilisation de trocarts de diamètre réduit afin de limiter la taille des incisions. Cette réduction du diamètre peut toutefois compliquer le passage des implants de grande taille, qui doivent être pliés ou enroulés pour franchir cet accès étroit. La capacité de ces implants à être insérés dans des trocarts de petit diamètre constitue ainsi un enjeu important pour leur utilisation en chirurgie mini-invasive.

L’équipe de biomécanique de Trévoux développe des modèles numériques permettant notamment de simuler l’insertion d’un renfort dans un trocart chirurgical, en soutien aux équipes R&D chargées du développement de nouveaux textiles. Toutefois, le niveau de validation de ces modèles, notamment concernant la réponse du textile pendant son insertion, reste limité en raison du manque de données expérimentales.

Titre du stage : Caractérisation, modélisation et simulation de l’insertion d’un renfort pariétal dans un trocart chirurgical.

Vos missions

Ce stage vise à coupler des mesures expérimentales avancées de la déformation 3D d’un renfort avec des simulations détaillées par éléments finis, afin de mener des analyses de sensibilité sur les forces d’insertion dans un trocart.

Dans le cadre de ce projet, vous serez amené(e) à travailler autour de deux axes principaux :

1. Étude expérimentale – Mesure de la déformation 3D

Mettre en place un banc de mesure expérimental (ex. : corrélation d’images numériques 3D ou suivi optique basé sur la microtomographie, µCT) afin de caractériser quantitativement les champs complets de déformation 3D de l’implant (enroulement, plissement, compaction locale) lors de son insertion dans un trocart.

Évaluer l’effet de la vitesse d’insertion et des conditions aux limites sur les modes de déformation spatiale.

2. Modélisation numérique et étude de sensibilité

Améliorer et recalibrer le modèle par éléments finis existant pour les prothèses herniaires testées expérimentalement, en utilisant les données de déformation 3D pour sa validation.

Réaliser des analyses de sensibilité systématiques afin d’étudier l’influence des paramètres structuraux sur les profils de force d’insertion et les états de déformation locale.

Résultats attendus

Ce projet apportera des connaissances scientifiques fondamentales sur les phénomènes mécaniques et tribologiques locaux se produisant lors du passage dans le trocart.

L’intégration des cinématiques expérimentales 3D dans les modèles par éléments finis permettra de faire progresser le développement d’un jumeau numérique validé et prédictif, contribuant ainsi à accélérer le développement des prothèses par les équipes d’ingénierie textile.

Les résultats de l’analyse de sensibilité serviront de guides de conception pour l’optimisation structurale des textiles chirurgicaux de nouvelle génération.

Votre profil

Vous êtes actuellement en dernière année d’école d’ingénieur ou en Master 2 (M2), avec une spécialisation en génie mécanique, biomécanique ou science des matériaux.

Vous disposez de connaissances en modélisation numérique, notamment en simulation par éléments finis (FEM), idéalement avec LS-DYNA et/ou Abaqus.

Vous avez des notions en traitement d’images médicales, segmentation et génération de maillages 3D.

Vous maîtrisez un logiciel de conception CAO, idéalement SolidWorks.

Vous avez des compétences en programmation scientifique, notamment sur Python et/ou MATLAB.

Vous possédez des connaissances en méthodes numériques et en outils de simulation et de calcul.

Une première expérience en modélisation numérique et simulation par éléments finis, acquise dans le cadre d’un stage ou d’un projet académique, serait appréciée.

Vous maîtrisez l’anglais, à l’écrit comme à l’oral, et êtes capable de mener des recherches bibliographiques scientifiques et de rédiger des rapports techniques en anglais.

Vos qualités personnelles

Vous faites preuve de rigueur et de précision dans votre travail.

Vous démontrez une bonne capacité d’adaptation.

Vous appréciez le travail en équipe et vous avez de bonnes capacités de communication.

Vous êtes autonome, organisé(e) et force de proposition

Durée et lieu :

Stage de 6 mois, à partir de février 2027.

Pourquoi Medtronic ?

Rejoignez un leader mondial des technologies médicales, où votre travail contribuera à l’excellence opérationnelle et à l’innovation. Bénéficiez d’une expérience pratique dans un environnement dynamique et bienveillant, et ayez un impact réel dès le premier jour.

Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. A Day in the Life
Join a multidisciplinary Research & Development (R&D) team focused on developing and sustaining innovative surgical platforms that support improved patient outcomes. This team is responsible for verification and validation of complex medical systems that integrate software, hardware, and algorithms while ensuring compliance with quality and regulatory standards.

As a Software Test Engineer, you will support the verification and validation of complex multidisciplinary medical systems. Working closely with Software, Systems Engineering, Quality, Regulatory, and Verification & Validation teams, you will execute system-level testing activities, investigate product issues, validate software performance, and contribute to maintaining high standards of product quality and compliance.

Primary Responsibilities:

Design, develop, and execute system-level software verification tests

Create and perform test cases validating software interactions within multidisciplinary medical systems

Verify end-to-end workflows, interfaces, data flow, and system behavior against product requirements

Analyze test results, identify trends and product risks, and document findings

Investigate defects, support root-cause analysis, validate fixes, and perform regression testing

Author test protocols, traceability documentation, and formal verification reports in compliance with quality and regulatory requirements

Develop and maintain test automation tools and scripts to improve testing efficiency and coverage

Support released-product activities including sustaining projects, corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs), software updates, and product enhancements

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, or related engineering discipline AND 2+ years of experience in software testing, verification and validation, algorithm validation, or system integration

Experience testing multidisciplinary systems that incorporate software, hardware, and algorithms

Experience developing and executing verification test plans, test cases, and test documentation

Knowledge of software defect investigation, root-cause analysis, and regression testing

Availability to work on-site in Caesarea at least 3 days per week

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience in the medical device or other regulated industry

Experience with test automation tools, scripting, or automation framework development

Programming skills and understanding of system integration concepts

Experience working with cross-functional engineering teams in product development or sustaining environments

Knowledge of quality system and regulatory requirements applicable to medical devices

CathWorks, recently acquired by Medtronic, is the leader in digital health innovations that improve the lives of patients globally. Responsibilities may include the following and other duties may be assigned:

Design, develop, maintain, and continuously improve AI, computer vision and image processing algorithms for a medical imaging product.

Own the full lifecycle of algorithm development, from concept and data definition through implementation, validation, product integration, and long-term maintenance.

Use both classical computer vision methods and machine/deep learning methods to come up with solutions for various problems in the domains of image classification, segmentation and 3D modeling.

Collaborate with SW developers, biomedical engineers, product specialists and other algorithms developers to refine and enhance existing applications.

Maintain and improve algorithm robustness, performance and reliability in production environments.

Identify opportunities for innovation and design novel algorithms to address complex technical challenges.

Stay at the forefront of relevant academic research by reviewing the latest papers and evaluating their potential impact on the company’s algorithmic stack.

Required Knowledge and Experience:

M.Sc. in computer science, electrical engineering, physics, mathematics, or related fields (excellent B.Sc. graduates will be considered as well).

5+ years of experience in developing and implementing AI, computer vision, and image processing algorithms.

Strong understanding of data quality, dataset design, model evaluation, and performance analysis.

Self-driven with the ability to independently lead technical projects from concept through deployment.

Experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow – an advantage.

Experience with MATLAB for algorithm development and analysis – an advantage.

Le site combine ainsi un fort savoir-faire industriel, des compétences avancées en métallurgie et une expertise en automatisation.

Définir, suivre et animer les indicateurs clés de performance du site.

Identifier les leviers d’amélioration et piloter les plans d’actions associés.

Promouvoir une culture d’amélioration continue basée sur les méthodologies Lean, Six Sigma et Operational Excellence.

Garantir la conformité du site avec les exigences réglementaires et normatives applicables aux dispositifs médicaux.

Veiller au respect des standards qualité du groupe et des exigences des autorités compétentes.

Assurer la robustesse des processus industriels, la maîtrise des changements et la gestion proactive des risques.

Piloter la préparation et le suivi des audits internes et externes ainsi que la mise en œuvre des actions correctives et préventives.

Fédérer les équipes autour d’objectifs communs, d’une culture de responsabilité et d’un haut niveau d’engagement.

Développer les talents, soutenir la montée en compétences et accompagner les managers dans leur développement.

Conduire les transformations organisationnelles nécessaires à l’évolution du site et à l’atteinte de ses ambitions.

Supporter la stratégie du site.

Soutenir les projets d’investissement, d’automatisation, de digitalisation et d’optimisation des flux.

Contribuer à l’industrialisation de nouveaux produits, procédés ou technologies.

Identifier les opportunités d’optimisation capacitaire, d’amélioration de la compétitivité et de sécurisation des opérations.

Participer à la construction des business cases relatifs aux investissements, aux évolutions d’organisation et aux projets de transformation.

Assurer une interface efficace avec les fonctions R&D, qualité, supply chain, affaires réglementaires, RH et finance.

Bonne connaissance des référentiels qualité (ISO 13485, Process Validation, IQOQPQ) et réglementaires applicables aux dispositifs médicaux.

Expérience dans un environnement industriel avec une forte présence syndicale, ainsi qu’une bonne connaissance du droit du travail et des règlementations sociales du pays.

Medtronic Clinical Research Solutions (MCRS) provides centralized clinical trial support services that help accelerate study execution while maintaining quality and compliance. Within the Site Activation & Support (SAS) organization, the Consents team partners with clinical Operating Units and cross-functional stakeholders to support informed consent development, review, and operational readiness for clinical research studies. The team works closely with Legal, Data Privacy, Compliance, Quality, and other clinical functions to help drive efficient site activation and study start-up activities.

As the Consents Manager for the Medtronic Clinical Research Solutions - Site Activation and Support (MCRS SAS), you will manage a team of US-based Informed Consent Specialists who provide consent-related services to Medtronic clinical Operating Units (OUs). This role is responsible for providing people leadership, operational oversight, and strategic direction for informed consent-related services supporting clinical research activities. In addition, the individual will serve as the business process owner for the Consents function, driving continuous improvement, standardization, and optimization of processes, tools, and systems.

The MCRS SAS organization includes several clinical teams, including Contracts, Consents, Start-Up Specialists, and Payments

This is a highly collaborative and visible role that partners closely with SAS leadership, clinical OU stakeholders, Legal, Data Privacy, Compliance, Quality, and other MCRS functions to support efficient site activation and delivery excellence.

This position is based in Minneapolis, Minnesota and follows an onsite work arrangement. Travel up to 10% may be required to support business needs, stakeholder engagement, and team collaboration.

Primary Responsibilities

Lead, coach, and develop a team of Informed Consent Specialists to drive performance, engagement, and professional growth.

Direct resource planning, workload management, and prioritization to ensure timely delivery of consent-related services.

Serve as the business process owner for the Consents function, driving standardization, optimization, and adoption of best practices.

Oversee informed consent standard operating procedures (SOPs) and associated Quality Management System (QMS) and non-QMS documentation.

Monitor operational metrics, analyze performance trends, and implement actions to improve service delivery, quality, and efficiency.

Partner with clinical Operating Units, Legal, Data Privacy, Compliance, Quality, and other stakeholders to resolve complex consent-related issues.

Manage escalations and provide guidance on complex operational challenges impacting study start-up and site activation activities.

Collaborate with Site Activation & Support leadership to improve processes, remove barriers, and reduce site activation cycle times while maintaining compliance and quality standards.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree with 5+ years of clinical research, clinical operations, site activation, study start-up, or related experience OR Advanced degree with 3+ years of clinical research, clinical operations, site activation, study start-up, or related experience.

Experience leading projects, processes, or operational activities within a regulated clinical research environment.

Experience managing cross-functional stakeholders and driving process improvement initiatives.

Experience analyzing operational metrics and using data to support business decisions and performance improvements.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior people management experience in clinical research.

Experience supporting informed consent processes, documentation, or governance activities in clinical trials.

Experience with Quality Management Systems (QMS), standard operating procedures, and compliance requirements.

System leadership. Lead systems engineering activities for complex, multidisciplinary medical-device programs and significant product changes.

Customer and clinical needs. Partner with Marketing, Clinical, Human Factors, Medical Safety, and field-facing teams to translate stakeholder needs, use cases, and use environments into clear system-level design inputs.

Architecture and interfaces. Define, evaluate, and maintain system architecture, functional decomposition, interfaces, operating modes, performance budgets, and key design trade-offs across hardware, software, firmware, disposables, and accessories.

Risk management. Integrate product safety, usability, reliability, cybersecurity, and software risk considerations into system design; ensure risk controls are appropriately implemented, traced, and verified.

Verification and validation. Establish system verification and validation strategies, including methods, acceptance criteria, test architecture, evidence plans, and resolution of system-level anomalies.

Technical reviews. Plan and lead architecture reviews, requirements reviews, design reviews, trade studies, and technical decision forums. Communicate conclusions, residual risks, and recommendations to project and functional leadership.

Problem solving. Lead cross-functional root-cause investigations and system-level troubleshooting for complex design, integration, field, manufacturing, supplier, and product-performance issues.

Lifecycle stewardship. Support design changes, component obsolescence, CAPA and corrective actions, regulatory commitments, supplier changes, product enhancements, and continuity-of-supply initiatives.

Technical influence. Serve as a technical authority who influences without direct authority, aligns global teams, and helps programs make balanced decisions across patient safety, quality, performance, cost, schedule, manufacturability, and serviceability.

Capability building. Mentor systems engineers and partner disciplines; create reusable methods, templates, models, and lessons learned that improve predictability and technical excellence.

External collaboration. Engage suppliers, consultants, laboratories, clinicians, and other external partners when specialized capabilities or system evidence are required.

System context, architecture, functional decomposition, use scenarios, and interface definitions

Technical trade studies, engineering analyses, performance budgets, and decision records

System verification and validation strategies, plans, protocols, reports, and anomaly dispositions

Formal design review content and objective evidence supporting phase or business decisions

Experience with cardiac electrophysiology, cardiac mapping, ablation energy delivery, therapeutic catheters, sheaths, generators, navigation or visualization systems, or related accessories.

Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

A Day in the Life
The Manager, Regulatory Affairs - Strategic Alliances leads regulatory support for ACM strategic alliance partners and serves as a primary regulatory interface across the partnership lifecycle. This leader translates commercial agreements and partner product roadmaps into global regulatory strategies and executable registration plans; coordinates execution through product design and regional Regulatory Affairs teams; enables accurate and timely partner communications; supports partner documentation requests and health authority questions; and drives resolution of complex integration, change, and market-access challenges. The Manager leads one direct report while delivering outcomes through broad cross-functional and regional influence. Demonstrated expertise in project or program management is highly valued in this role.

A Day in the Life

Responsibilities may include the following and other duties may be assigned.

Partner Regulatory Strategy & Registration Planning

Serve as the named Regulatory Affairs point of contact for assigned strategic alliance partners, developing trusted relationships and maintaining continuity of agreement context, product history, and regulatory commitments.

Translate partnership agreements, commercial priorities, product roadmaps, technical integration plans, and launch objectives into global regulatory strategies, milestones, dependencies, and executable registration plans.

Clarify Medtronic and partner regulatory roles, deliverables, decision rights, documentation expectations, and escalation pathways for each program and market.

Identify regulatory risks, sequencing constraints, and market-access opportunities early enough to influence product, evidence, investment, integration, and launch decisions.

Maintain forward-looking registration roadmaps and forecasts that align partner demand with regional capacity, product readiness, and business priorities.

Global Execution, Monitoring & Partner Updates

Drive execution of agreed registration plans through product design and regional Regulatory Affairs teams and cross-functional partners, without duplicating regional submission ownership.

Establish operating rhythms, trackers, milestones, dashboards, and governance forums that provide clear visibility to progress, upcoming decisions, risks, and overdue actions.

Provide partners with accurate, timely, and audience-appropriate updates on registration status, constraints, decisions, and recovery plans.

Anticipate execution gaps, escalate issues with clear options and recommendations, and coordinate accountable action plans through closure.

Monitor performance and use lessons learned to improve forecasting, planning accuracy, responsiveness, and partner experience.

Partner Portal, Documentation & Health Authority Support

Own the Regulatory Affairs intake, triage, prioritization, and coordination of partner portal requests for registration documentation and regulatory information.

Coordinate with product, regional, quality, clinical, engineering, operations, legal, and other subject matter experts to provide complete, consistent, controlled, and timely responses.

Support partners as they pursue global registrations, including responding to questions from health authorities and coordinating supplemental documentation or technical clarification.

Maintain request records, documentation traceability, partner-specific knowledge, and appropriate access controls within the portal and related systems.

Identify recurring requests and develop standardized content, guidance, or self-service solutions that improve efficiency while protecting compliance and confidential information.

Issue Resolution, Change Assessment & Integration Support

Lead cross-functional troubleshooting when partner registrations or integrations encounter barriers, ambiguity, or misalignment.

Coordinate resolution of issues involving product release readiness, system configuration, regulatory data, documentation inconsistencies, submission dependencies, and regional requirements.

Assess or coordinate regulatory impact assessments for product and process changes, partner product change notifications, evolving regulations and standards, and sustaining activities.

Facilitate fact-based decisions across Medtronic, partner, and regional stakeholders; document decisions, owners, actions, and residual risks.

Escalate significant compliance, contractual, market-access, timeline, or business-continuity risks to the appropriate governance body.

People & Stakeholder Leadership

Lead, coach, and develop one direct report, establishing clear responsibilities, priorities, performance expectations, and development objectives.

Allocate work between the leader and direct report based on partner complexity, risk, business priority, and capability development needs.

Build strong relationships with Strategic Alliance Sales, Quality, R&D, Operations, Marketing, Legal, Supply Chain, and partner organizations.

Communicate complex regulatory topics clearly across executive, partner, regional, and technical audiences and influence outcomes without relying on formal authority.

Promote an inclusive, accountable, responsive, and continuous-improvement culture focused on partner commitments, patient access, and compliant execution.

Must Have: Minimum Requirements

Baccalaureate degree in science, engineering, regulatory affairs, or a related discipline and a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience, including 3+ years of leadership experience demonstrated through direct management and/or significant mentorship or advisory responsibility; or an advanced degree with a minimum of 3 years of relevant experience, including 3+ years of leadership experience.

Demonstrated medical device regulatory experience supporting global registrations, product lifecycle activities, product changes, or market-access programs.

Experience leading complex, cross-functional programs in a regulated, global, and matrixed environment.

Experience translating strategy into structured plans, milestones, governance, risk management, and consistent execution.

Ability to communicate and influence effectively with internal leaders, regional teams, technical experts, and external business partners.

Nice to Have

Advanced degree in science, engineering, regulatory affairs, business, law, or a related discipline.

Experience supporting OEM, distributor, licensing, co-development, integration, or other strategic alliance business models.

Experience developing global regulatory strategies and coordinating registrations across multiple international markets.

Experience managing partner portals, request-management processes, controlled documentation, regulatory information systems, dashboards, or workflow tools.

Experience assessing product changes, product change notifications, system or configuration changes, standards transitions, and documentation discrepancies.

Working knowledge of design controls, product release, quality systems, labeling, and post-market regulatory obligations.

Strong business acumen, customer orientation, negotiation, conflict resolution, presentation, and executive communication skills.

Demonstrated success developing talent and improving team operating mechanisms.

For Baccalaureate degrees earned outside of the United States, a degree that satisfies the requirements of 8 C.F.R. § 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A) is required.

The Employee & Labour Relations (ELR) function provides specialised support to leaders, managers, and employees on workplace matters, ensuring consistent application of employment practices, policies, and labour law requirements. This role serves as the primary ELR partner for North Africa and the Middle East, partnering with Human Resources Business Partners, Legal & Compliance, and business leaders to manage employee relations matters, organisational change initiatives, and workplace investigations.

This position is based in Cairo, Egypt. The role supports multiple countries across the region and requires close collaboration with stakeholders in a matrix organisation.
As the Employee & Labour Relations Partner for North Africa and the Middle East, you will provide expert guidance on employee relations matters, employment practices, workplace investigations, performance improvement, restructuring activities, and conflict resolution. The role partners closely with business leaders, Human Resources, and Legal teams to address complex workplace issues while ensuring compliance with local employment legislation and company policies. Deep knowledge and expertise in the Egyptian labour law will be critical to be successful in this role.

Primary Responsibilities:

Lead employee relations case management, including disciplinary matters, workplace concerns, performance issues, investigations, and involuntary terminations.

Advise and coach leaders on employee relations practices, policy interpretation, performance management, and organisational restructuring activities.

Conduct workplace investigations in partnership with Legal & Compliance, gathering documentation, assessing findings, and supporting resolution plans.

Facilitate conflict resolution through mediation, coaching, and other workplace intervention techniques.

Manage restructuring programmes and workforce transition activities, ensuring compliance with local employment requirements.

Maintain accurate and timely case documentation within the Employee Relations Case Management System (ServiceNow).

Partner with Human Resources Business Partners and Centres of Expertise to address organisational effectiveness and workforce-related challenges.

Ensure consistent application of company policies, employment practices, and regional labour legislation while maintaining confidentiality of sensitive employee information.

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree and 5+ years of experience in employee relations, labour relations, human resources, or employment law.

Experience in Egyptian Labour law and the ability to work autonomously in relation to these matters.

Experience managing employee relations cases, workplace investigations, disciplinary processes, and performance improvement programmes.

Experience supporting employee and labour relations activities across multiple countries within North Africa and the Middle East.

Experience interpreting human resources policies and applying country-specific employment legislation.

Experience partnering with business leaders across multiple stakeholder groups.

Experience leading restructuring initiatives, workforce transitions, or reduction-in-force programmes.

Fluent written and verbal English communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience using ServiceNow or similar case management systems.

Experience partnering with Legal & Compliance teams on employment investigations and risk mitigation.

Experience within a multinational healthcare, medical technology, or highly regulated industry environment.

The Neuromodulation and Pelvic Health R&D organizations, bring together a large set of Medtronic’s Neurosciences therapies and their project teams to employ the full breadth of our talent, technologies, products, services, and solutions to address the needs of customers and patients across the globe. These operating units offer devices and therapies to treat chronic pain, movement disorders, overactive bladder, non-obstructive urinary retention, and much more.

The Senior Product Security Engineer – Embedded IoT is responsible for cybersecurity architecture and Security-by-Design for implantable and connected medical-device platforms. The role focuses on embedded systems, device connectivity, cryptography, secure provisioning, firmware updates, and protection of device-to-device and device-to-edge communication.

Primary Responsibilities

Embedded & IoT Security Architecture

Define security architecture and requirements for implantable devices, programmers/controllers, gateways, and connected operating environments.

Apply Security-by-Design and Defense-in-Depth across hardware, firmware, communication interfaces, authentication, authorization, and data protection.

Design secure boot, HSM/secure-element integration, encryption, key management, device identity, and secure provisioning.

Threat Modeling & Security Risk

Lead threat modeling, Security Risk Analysis, attack-surface analysis, and security requirements definition throughout the device lifecycle.

Translate identified threats into architectural controls, product security requirements, verification activities, and risk-control evidence.

Maintain SBOM and software/component security requirements for embedded platforms.

Connected Device Security

Define secure communication architecture for BLE, wired/wireless interfaces, programmers, gateways, and remote-monitoring connectivity.

Support secure eFOTA/firmware update architecture including signing, authentication, anti-rollback, integrity verification, and recovery.

Define manufacturing security requirements for device identity, cryptographic key/certificate injection, provisioning, and lifecycle management.

Compliance & Product Development

Integrate cybersecurity requirements into systems, software, hardware, manufacturing, verification, and risk-management processes.

Support regulatory submissions and compliance with medical-device cybersecurity standards and guidance.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in related field with 4 years of relevant experience OR masters degree in related field with 2 years of relevant experience (Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Cybersecurity)

Extensive experience in embedded security, IoT security, firmware, connected devices, or medical-device development.

Preferred Qualifications

Strong knowledge of cryptography, HSM/secure elements, PKI, secure boot, provisioning, firmware signing, BLE/network security, and embedded secure development.

Experience with threat modeling, Security Risk Assessment, SBOM, Security-by-Design, Defense-in-Depth, and regulated product development.

Understanding of medical device regulations and standards (e.g., FDA pre- and post-market guidance on cybersecurity for medical device manufacturers, ISO 13485, ISO 81001-5-1).

Strong decision-making capabilities, weighing relative costs and benefits to identify the most appropriate solution.

High attention to detail with a focus on Good Documentation Practices (GDP).

Ability to communicate complex, technical information in a creative and engaging way to diverse audiences, orally and in writing.

Excellent prioritization skills, with an aptitude for breaking down work into manageable parts and assessing priority and time required.

Demonstrated ability to develop and grow productive, trusting, and open relationships with a wide variety of constituencies.

Physics of Failure

6-Sigma

The Principal Mechanical Engineer in Electrophysiology Technologies (EPT) serves as a recognized technical authority responsible for the architecture, design, verification, and lifecycle support of complex electromechanical systems used in cardiac mapping and ablation therapies. The role provides technical leadership across released product engineering and technology innovation, with a strong focus on patient safety, product reliability, regulatory compliance, risk management, and sustainable product performance.

Operating with a high degree of autonomy and ownership, the Principal Engineer identifies and drives technical priorities, provides direction across multiple programs, mentors engineers, and influences cross-functional decisions involving systems, firmware, electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, quality, regulatory, and supplier teams. The role is expected to anticipate risks, resolve ambiguity, make sound engineering decisions, and drive complex issues through implementation and closure.

Primary Responsibilities:

Own and drive mechanical engineering activities for released products, from problem definition and technical assessment through design implementation, verification, release, and post-implementation monitoring.

Develop and implement mechanical design improvements that enhance patient safety, product performance, system reliability, serviceability, and scalable manufacturing.

Provide technical leadership for complex, ambiguous, or high-risk product and process issues; establish investigation strategies, make evidence-based decisions, and ensure actions are driven to effective closure.

Lead cross-functional technical teams in investigating product and process issues, applying structured root-cause analysis to define, implement, and verify effective corrective and preventive actions.

Apply sound engineering fundamentals, analytical methods, tolerance analysis, material selection, and design verification techniques to support robust mechanical solutions.

Create and review 3D models, engineering drawings, specifications, technical reports, and presentations; ensure design outputs are complete, accurate, and suitable for release.

Design, qualify, document, and maintain test fixtures, jigs, and tools, and provide technical oversight for associated testing activities.

Lead or support test method development and validation, design verification and validation, and the interpretation and communication of results.

Integrate risk-based decision-making and Design for Reliability and Manufacturability principles throughout design and development activities.

Own timely, high-quality completion of applicable design control deliverables, technical reviews, product configuration activities, and engineering changes.

Collaborate with program management, Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory, Systems, Electrical, Firmware, and external suppliers on component selection, manufacturing processes, assembly methods, and product improvements.

Investigate audit findings, process flows, and systemic gaps, and translate findings into practical, sustainable engineering improvements.

Partner with Quality as a primary technical point of contact during internal and external audits and provide clear, evidence-based responses.

Present technical findings, recommendations, risks, and project status clearly to cross-functional teams, senior management, and governance forums through design reviews, reports, presentations, and other appropriate communication channels.

Mentor and technically develop engineers at multiple experience levels, reinforcing engineering rigor, mechanical design best practices, effective documentation, problem solving, and accountability.

Influence engineering standards, design guidelines, platform strategies, and technology roadmaps within EPT.

Represent mechanical engineering expertise in program reviews, technical escalations, and governance forums, and constructively challenge decisions when technical evidence or patient safety considerations warrant further action.

Maintain current knowledge of relevant technologies, standards, industry practices, and emerging engineering methods, and apply that knowledge to improve products and processes.

Travel to suppliers and design or manufacturing sites as required.

Required Knowledge and Experience:

Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or a related engineering discipline with at least seven years of relevant experience; or a master’s degree with at least five years of relevant experience; or a PhD with at least three years of relevant experience.

Demonstrated technical depth in the design, analysis, verification, and lifecycle support of complex mechanical or electromechanical products.

Experience designing highly precise machined components, sheet-metal components, and mechanical assemblies.

Proficiency with 3D CAD and engineering drawing tools, such as SolidWorks.

Strong knowledge of metal and plastic materials, component manufacturing processes, tolerancing, assembly methods, and design for manufacturability.

Knowledge of engineering change management, configuration control, and product lifecycle management tools such as Agile or Windchill.

Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical work with limited direction, manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgment, and take ownership from problem identification through closure.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including structured root-cause analysis, technical risk assessment, and data-driven decision-making.

Ability to communicate complex technical information clearly and influence decisions across functions and organizational levels.

Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams in a multinational matrix organization while maintaining accountability for technical outcomes.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience in the medical device industry, particularly with safety-critical capital equipment or electromechanical systems.

Working knowledge of medical device quality systems, design controls, and applicable standards and regulations, including 21 CFR Part 820 and ISO 13485.

Experience with process validation and equipment qualification, including IQ, OQ, and PQ activities.

Experience applying IEC 60601-1 requirements to medical electrical equipment.

Experience with medical device labeling or symbol requirements, including ISO 15223-1.

Experience with product risk management in accordance with ISO 14971.

Experience conducting product or process investigations and supporting corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs).

Experience providing technical leadership during audits, regulatory inspections, or complex quality-system investigations.

Master of Science degree.

Experience with laser welding, cutting, texturing, marking, ablation, micro-machining, or related laser-material processing technologies.

Experience with parallel-gap welding, step-gap welding, or other precision joining processes.

Experience supporting implantable medical devices, miniature assemblies, or other highly regulated, high-reliability products.

Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. A Day in the Life
At Medtronic Neuroscience, we bring innovation, expertise, and purpose together to improve outcomes and transform lives for people living with neurological, spine, and chronic pain conditions.

Our Neurovascular Operating Unit advances stroke and cerebrovascular care through innovative, minimally invasive technologies that enable rapid, life-saving intervention. From restoring blood flow to securing complex vascular conditions, our solutions help clinicians achieve better outcomes when every second counts.

Check us out on LinkedIn: Medtronic Neurovascular

In this role, the Senior Quality Engineer will provide engineering leadership for the evaluation and resolution of post-market product quality and safety issues across the Neurovascular portfolio. The engineer will apply product design knowledge, engineering analysis, risk management, statistics, and data analytics to characterize device performance, investigate field-reported failure modes, determine root cause, and assess potential patient and product impact. This role partners closely with R&D, Manufacturing Engineering, Supplier Quality, Regulatory, Clinical, and Operations to translate post-market signals into technically sound risk controls, product improvements, and sustained product reliability while ensuring compliance with applicable regulatory requirements.

Join a diverse team of innovators who bring their worldview, their unique backgrounds and their individual life experiences to work every day. It’s no accident – we work hard to cultivate a workforce that reflects our patients and partners. We believe it’s the only way to drive healthcare forward and remain a global leader in medical technology and solutions.

This position is on-site in Irvine, CA 4 days/week, with the option to work 1 day/week of your choosing remote.

Responsibilities:

Engineering Investigation and Issue Resolution:

Lead engineering evaluations of post-market complaints and product performance signals, including assessment of device failure modes, use conditions, patient impact, and potential product risk.

Plan and lead complex technical investigations using engineering problem-solving methods, product and process knowledge, returned-device analysis, test data, manufacturing records, and supplier information.

Develop and document technically supported root cause and failure-mechanism conclusions, including clear evaluation of evidence, limitations, and residual uncertainty.

Partner with R&D, Manufacturing Engineering, Supplier Quality, Regulatory, Clinical, Marketing, and Operations to define containment, product controls, corrective actions, and design or process improvements based on investigation findings.

Product Risk and Post-Market Engineering:

Apply design control and risk management principles throughout the product lifecycle to evaluate whether post-market information changes known hazards, failure modes, risk estimates, or the adequacy of existing controls.

Review and develop engineering test strategies, protocols, methods, and reports to ensure evaluations are technically appropriate, statistically sound, and sufficient to support quality and regulatory decisions.

Perform complaint trending, signal detection, and data analysis to identify emerging product performance issues and distinguish meaningful signals from expected variation.

The Cardiac Rhythm Management (CRM) portfolio delivers therapies designed to restore, support, and protect every heartbeat through advanced pacing, defibrillation, and remote monitoring solutions. CRM's unique ability to pair proven life-saving therapies with intelligent technology gives clinicians and patients greater confidence. Clinical impact and innovation come together to improve lives through meaningful patient outcomes.

We push the limits of what technology can do to make tomorrow better than yesterday. The Cardiac Rhythm Management Electrical System Design team develops electronics, integration approaches, and engineering solutions that enable life-saving implantable and external medical device systems.

As a Senior Electrical Engineering Manager, you will help shape the Electrical System Design functional strategy and translate that direction into actionable plans for your team. Working with R&D leadership, you will anticipate future product needs, identify gaps in expertise and infrastructure, and recommend priorities for capability development and technical investment. You will balance program delivery with the long-term strength of the function, aligning team capabilities and technical priorities with business needs.

You will lead a team of 10–15 engineers, ranging from entry-level engineers to experienced technical leaders and subject matter experts, supporting multiple product platforms and concurrent development programs. The team works across the full product lifecycle, from architecture and requirements definition through circuit and PCB design, firmware and ASIC integration, characterization, verification, manufacturing transfer, and post-market support.

You will be accountable for the team’s technical execution, organizational health, and employee engagement. This includes developing technical talent and leadership capability and partnering with program management and cross-functional leaders to align resources and commitments with business priorities.

This role is ideal for an experienced engineering leader who is passionate about developing people and delivering complex medical technologies that improve patients’ lives.

This position is located in Mounds View, MN (Twin Cities Metro).

The Electrical System Design team is responsible for delivering high-reliability, safety-critical electrical designs for active implantable cardiac devices and associated external systems. The team works across the full product development lifecycle, including architecture definition, requirements development, circuit and PCB design, firmware and ASIC integration, design characterization, verification, production test development, manufacturing transfer, and post-market support.

The Senior Electrical Engineering Manager contributes to the development of the Electrical System Design functional strategy and translates that direction into actionable plans for the team. Working with R&D leadership, this manager anticipates future product needs, identifies gaps in expertise and infrastructure, and recommends priorities for capability development and technical investment. The manager balances program delivery with the long-term strength of the function and is accountable for the team’s technical execution, organizational health, and employee engagement. This includes developing technical talent and leadership capability and partnering with program management and R&D leaders to align resources and commitments with business priorities.

Responsibilities may include the following and other duties may be assigned.

Defines and advances the electrical engineering functional strategy, including technical capability development, engineering methods and tools, and investments needed to support current and future product portfolios.

Recruits, develops, coaches, and evaluates team members; establishes clear goals aligned with business and program objectives; and provides ongoing performance feedback, career development, and technical leadership opportunities.

Builds an inclusive, high-performing team culture grounded in technical excellence, accountability, design rigor, collaboration, and knowledge sharing, while developing the capabilities needed to support current and future programs.

Owns resource planning, prioritization, and staffing across product development programs, sustaining projects, and functional initiatives, balancing near-term commitments with long-term capability needs and escalating resource gaps and competing priorities.

Partners with program managers and cross-functional leaders to establish electrical engineering commitments aligned with program cost, scope, and schedule objectives; monitors execution against those commitments; and drives corrective actions and technical risk mitigation as needed.

Ensures the team delivers robust electrical designs and PCB implementations supported by clear requirements, interface specifications, design documentation, and well-defined characterization and verification strategies; ensures resulting evidence demonstrates compliance with product requirements and applicable medical device design controls.

Leads electrical system integration across PCB hardware, ASICs, firmware, mechanical interfaces, and telemetry/RF systems, ensuring compatibility with manufacturing processes and alignment with product requirements.

Ensures appropriate technical expertise and rigorous reviews are applied to circuit and PCB design, mixed-signal electronics, RF/telemetry performance, EMI/EMC, MRI safety, reliability, and safety-critical design decisions.

Guides issue resolution, root-cause analysis, and technical decision-making for complex development and manufacturing issues, including tradeoffs involving power consumption, sensing performance, device size, reliability, manufacturability, and product cost.

A Day in the Life

Together, we can change healthcare worldwide which is why we’re embarking on a new venture in Malaysia and want you to be a part the next generation of life-changing medical technology to patients worldwide by being a part of our next chapter of innovation in Malaysia.

Medtronic is intensely focused on creating a workplace environment which reflects our standing as the world’s top medical device company. The ideal candidate will have a passion for the patients we serve and an unrelenting commitment to our new venture in Malaysia.

In this exciting role as a Senior Quality Engineer, you will be responsible for driving the transfer of manufacturing processes and products from our established facility to the new manufacturing site. While you will ensure that quality standards and protocols are effectively applied and maintained throughout the transfer process, aligning with ISO 13485 requirements and the company’s Quality Management System (QMS), you will have the unique and amazing opportunity to be a team player in a global team applying design flow down and transfer experience.

This role requires strong technical judgment and ownership of quality strategy during manufacturing transfer. You will be reporting to the Senior Quality Manager and works closely within a cross-functional team including design and research, engineering, manufacturing, legal manufacturers, and supply chain to ensure successful and compliant manufacturing transfers.

This position is based fully on-site at our new local facility. International travel of +25% may be required during the transfer project interacting with the sending site team and supporting key transfer activities at both sending and receiving sites.

Primary Responsibilities:

Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior quality engineers and cross-functional teams throughout the transfer process.

Develop, modify, apply, and maintain quality standards and protocols for transferring products and manufacturing processes, ensuring compliance with ISO 13485:2016 and the company’s Quality Management System (QMS).

Collaborate with cross-functional teams including engineering, manufacturing, regulatory, supply chain, and suppliers to integrate quality requirements into all phases of the transfer plan, from process setup through production handover.

Define and implement inspection methods, sampling plans, and quality controls for transferred processes, including in-process and final inspection stages.

Support Test Method Validation (TMV), process validation activities (IQ/OQ/PQ), ensuring protocols, acceptance criteria, and documentation meet regulatory and QMS requirements.

Ensure quality engineering activities for NPI manufacturing transfer are compliant with quality requirements, including traceability of DOTM, process validations, etc.

Develop and maintain process risk management documentation (PFMEA, control plans) to identify, mitigate, and monitor process risks during transfer and production ramp-up.

Coordinate readiness of manufacturing equipment, tooling, and inspection systems to support process qualification and production start-up.

Work with the sending site and local teams to collect and analyze historical quality data, defect trends, and process capability information to proactively address known risks before production launch.

Participate in readiness reviews, special builds, and verification activities to ensure process capability, product quality, and yield targets are met.

Review and manage quality issues (e.g. nonconformances) during transfer builds, ensuring timely closure, root cause analysis, and escalation into CAPA when required.

Ensure audit readiness by maintaining complete, accurate, and compliant records for validation, inspection, and risk management activities.

Apply continuous improvement principles and implement structured problem-solving tools to drive issue resolution, waste elimination, and process optimization throughout the product transfer lifecycle.

Focus on enhancing process stability, improving efficiency, and sustaining high-quality output post-transfer.

Encourage a culture of First Time Quality at the Source, emphasizing preventive and predictive approaches to minimize defects and ensure compliance from the start.

Required Qualifications:

A university degree in engineering (biomedical, chemical, industrial, biotechnology, or related fields) is required and minimum of 6 years of relevant experience.

Experience in regulated industries such as medical devices, pharmaceuticals, or biotechnology is necessary.

Proficiency in preparing and reviewing technical documentation, including protocols, reports, and validations, is essential.

Knowledge of ISO 13485 quality management system requirements must be demonstrated.

A good understanding of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) is important.

Intermediate to advanced English skills, especially for reading and writing technical documents, are needed.

Clear verbal and written communication abilities are required.

Experience with creating and maintaining SOPs, protocols, and technical reports is essential.

Willingness to travel as per job requirements is necessary.

Holding a valid passport for travel purposes is mandatory.

Willingness to undertake extended overseas assignments of one month or more, if needed, is expected.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience working with cross-functional teams such as production, quality, regulatory, and engineering adds value.

At Medtronic, we bring bold ideas forward with speed and decisiveness to put patients first in everything we do. In-person exchanges are invaluable to our work. We’re working a minimum of 4 days a week onsite as part of our commitment to fostering a culture of professional growth and cross-functional collaboration as we work together to engineer the extraordinary.

Medtronic’s Acute Care & Monitoring (ACM) business is focused on empowering clinicians with monitoring tools that deliver timely insights and improve patient care across hospital and post-acute settings. Connectivity is the backbone of this transformation, enabling devices, data, and teams to work together as one ecosystem.

Within ACM, the HealthCast™ portfolio represents our digital health solutions across wearables, remote monitoring, connectivity, and services. The market for connected care is growing quickly, with real potential to reshape how patients are monitored and how care teams collaborate. Are you ready to help lead how we bring that to life.

As the Global Product Marketing Manager – Connectivity on the Digital Health team, you’ll be at the center of that mission, leading global downstream strategy and lifecycle management for the solutions that power ACM’s connectivity infrastructure, ensuring clinicians have access to the insights they need when and where they need them.

Why This Role Matters

Connectivity is transforming healthcare by ensuring data flows seamlessly between devices, systems, and care teams. In this role you’ll turn that potential into reality, globalizing how we deliver connectivity, amplifying Medtronic’s voice in the market, and ensuring customer insights shape what comes next.
